## Tours to Tenorio National Park and the Río Celeste river

[Tenorio National Park](/costa-rica/place/tenorio-volcano-national-park/) lies in northern [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) and protects humid tropical forest around a volcanic massif. Visitors come to see one of the country's most distinctive natural landscapes: the vivid blue water of [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/), a waterfall surrounded by dense greenery, and the confluence known as Los Teñideros.

Unlike roadside sightseeing stops, a visit to Tenorio involves **walking along a nature trail**. The particular day of your visit, the journey from your previous overnight stop, the level of exertion and what follows the park all matter when choosing a tour. Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. All visit Tenorio as part of the main itinerary, but differ in length and geography.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries include Tenorio?

### 7 days: from Arenal and Caño Negro to the ocean

["Costa Rica: Short but Complete"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/) lasts **7 days**. The journey begins around San José and Poás Volcano before continuing through [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/) to Río Celeste. The Tamarindo coast follows.

**Day 3** features a walk through Tenorio National Park's forest with an ecological guide, visiting Los Teñideros and the Río Celeste waterfall. This itinerary suits travellers who want to experience volcanic areas, wetlands and beaches within one week. The schedule is fairly full, so it should not be mistaken for several days devoted solely to Tenorio.

### 9 days: volcanic landscapes, Maleku culture and the coast

["Costa Rica: Beaches and Mountains"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-beaches-mountains/) is a **9-day** journey. It begins in [Liberia](/costa-rica/place/liberia/) and [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/). Travellers then head to the Tenorio area, discover the culture of the Maleku people, continue through Arenal and [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), and spend the final days by the Pacific.

On **day 3**, the programme includes a guided forest hike and a visit to Los Teñideros, followed by accommodation at Tenorio Lodge. This arrangement allows time to experience Tenorio while moving between volcanic regions, rather than treating it merely as a short stop en route to the beach.

The nine-day tour starts in a different geographical area from the seven-day version, with a more prominent role for the country's northwest. When comparing them, the sequence of stops and overnight stays matters more than simply adding two days to the shorter itinerary.

### 12 days: a VIP journey through Costa Rica and Nicaragua

The [Costa Rica and Nicaragua VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/) lasts **12 days**. It combines two countries, with a programme centred on nature, volcanic landscapes and culture. **Day 4** includes an excursion to Río Celeste in Tenorio National Park: the forest trail, Los Teñideros, the waterfall and a return to Hotel el Silencio after the walk.

This option is worth considering if you want to include the park in a larger journey that visits neighbouring Nicaragua. The tour title mentions a private plane, but **check the conditions for the specific flights, accommodation and guiding in the itinerary**. VIP status alone does not mean an aircraft takes you to Tenorio or that services not listed in the tour are available.

### 16 days: an extensive nature itinerary through Costa Rica

The [premium 16-day tour](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) devotes **day 5** to Río Celeste and Tenorio. In the morning, the journey heads towards the river, followed by a walk through humid forest to Los Teñideros and the waterfall. The description specifies that this is a walk rather than a demanding volcano ascent.

Travellers then visit Monteverde, [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/), [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) and Caño Island, finishing at [Playa Conchal](/costa-rica/place/playa-conchal/). The tour combines Tenorio with the wildlife of the southern Pacific coast and several days relaxing by the sea. The published tour description specifies a **private format**.

## What to see in Tenorio in one day

The park's principal visitor trail is called **Misterios del Tenorio**. According to the SINAC conservation authority, it is approximately 3 km long one way; the full return walk covers around **6 km** and takes roughly **3 hours**. These figures describe the park trail itself; they are not a promise that every Ada Tours programme visits every lookout along it.

| Place on the trail | Main highlight |
|---|---|
| Río Celeste Waterfall | Turquoise water amid the forest |
| Los Teñideros | The river's colour transformation |
| Blue Lagoon | Intense blue colour |
| Borbollones | Signs of volcanic activity |
| Viewpoint | View of the volcanic massif |

The Río Celeste waterfall is the park's best-known sight, reached by a trail through humid forest. Los Teñideros is the place where 2 streams meet and the change in water colour becomes visible. Other sections feature the Blue Lagoon and escaping volcanic gases. Access to individual sections depends on current rules and trail conditions.

**Swimming in the river inside the national park is prohibited.** This also applies to the inviting-looking blue sections. Tenorio is a destination for nature walks, observation and photographs, not water sports in the lagoon.

## Why is Río Celeste blue?

Río Celeste is famous for an unusual optical effect. At Los Teñideros, streams with different physical and chemical properties mix, and suspended mineral particles scatter light, making the water appear exceptionally blue. Researchers at the University of Costa Rica have linked the blue colour to light scattering by aluminosilicate particles. Los Teñideros is where the change is especially apparent.

Local stories tell of God washing his paintbrush in the river after painting the sky. The legend is part of the region's cultural tradition. The scientific explanation involves processes in the water, not the presence of blue dye. The intensity of the colour may vary with lighting and after heavy rainfall.

Similarly beautiful blue water can be found in some locations outside the main tourist trail, but these are different places with different access rules. If your priority is the forest trail and waterfall, check that the itinerary includes **Tenorio National Park**, rather than only a general visit to the river.

## Combining Tenorio with Arenal and Monteverde

Tenorio is usually combined with other natural regions of northern Costa Rica. [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) is known for its volcanic cone, solidified lava fields, hot springs and hanging bridges. Tenorio offers a more focused hike towards the blue river. The experiences complement each other, although both belong to the country's volcanic landscape.

[Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) has high-altitude cloud forests and different walking conditions. It is a useful addition for those who want to see how vegetation changes. [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/) is better suited to observing birds and wetland wildlife, including river excursions. These environments are markedly different from Tenorio's forest trail.

On a 7–9-day journey, you normally need to choose parks carefully to leave time for the beach. A 16-day programme allows you to visit many more of the country's natural regions. If hiking through natural landscapes is your main goal, explore [Costa Rica adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/costa-rica/), [wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/) and the full [country tour catalogue](/costa-rica/tour/).

## When to visit and how to prepare

Tenorio lies in a very humid region. Rain can begin even when other parts of Costa Rica are sunny. Wet rocks and steps become slippery, so choose closed shoes with good traction, bring light rain protection and keep electronics in a waterproof case.

**Admission to the park requires a ticket**, sold by SINAC through its official online system. Check current hours, visitor limits and trail conditions shortly before travelling. As of October 2026, the park's official page specifies admission beginning in the morning and a restricted afternoon entry window. Prices are deliberately not fixed in this article: admission rules are separate from the published conditions of any particular tour.

The physical difficulty depends on how much of the trail you walk. The route involves forest terrain, changes in elevation and stairways, so it is not a flat city path. However, **visitors do not need to climb to the summit of Tenorio Volcano** on the tourist trail. Where an Ada Tours itinerary specifies a guided walk, the day's conditions determine the actual exertion and stops covered.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Tenorio

### Can you see Río Celeste Waterfall without a long hike?

You need to follow part of the forest trail, including steps, to reach the waterfall. It is not a sight you can see in full from a car. The walking time depends on the accessible section, trail conditions and the group's pace.

### How much time should be allowed for Tenorio?

The park's official out-and-back trail takes approximately **3 hours** over **6 km**. Add the drive to the entrance, ticket checks, photography and rest. The length of the actual touring day depends on the Ada Tours itinerary, not only on the trail distance.

### Can you swim in the blue water?

Entering the river and swimming inside the national park is prohibited. Visitors come to Río Celeste and the waterfall for the scenery and walk.

### How is Tenorio different from Arenal?

[Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) is best known for its volcanic landscape and geothermal areas. Tenorio's defining experience is the blue river amid humid forest and the place where its colour changes. Both can fit into the same journey.

### Which itinerary devotes a separate day to Tenorio?

All 4 tours discussed here include a dedicated stage for Río Celeste and Tenorio: **day 3** on the 7- and 9-day programmes, **day 4** on the 12-day VIP itinerary and **day 5** on the 16-day journey. That does not mean an entire day is spent inside the park; travel and other activities are also involved.

### Which trip is best for a first visit to Costa Rica?

If you only have a week, choose the seven-day itinerary if you are comfortable with a busy programme and several transfers. For more time combining natural regions and the coast, consider the nine-day tour. The 12- and 16-day journeys cover a wider area: Nicaragua or Costa Rica's southern Pacific coast, respectively.

## Tortuguero: canals, sea turtles and a journey into Costa Rica's Caribbean rainforest

Tortuguero National Park is on the northeastern Caribbean coast of [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/). Instead of conventional roads through the forest, rivers and canals form the routes; boats are part of everyday transport and green banks often limit visibility to just a few metres. It is one of the country's most rewarding places to observe tropical wildlife from the water.

There are two principal reasons to visit: **the canal ecosystem** and **the sea turtle nesting season**. These activities differ in their timing, access arrangements and the chances of a sighting. Boat trips operate in various months, while turtle watching requires the appropriate season, compliance with conservation rules and valid authorisation.

Tortuguero should not be treated as an ordinary Caribbean beach resort. The SINAC park authority warns of dangerous currents and advises against swimming in the sea or lagoons. The park's beaches are valuable above all as protected habitat for wildlife.

## Tortuguero's canals: what can you see from a boat?

Boat routes follow dense vegetation, flooded forest and banks where waterbirds, iguanas, caimans and monkeys may be spotted. The difference between a rewarding wildlife excursion and a quick trip from A to B is the pace: spotting animals means stopping, scanning branches, listening and keeping quiet.

SINAC identifies several waterways, including **Río Tortuguero**, **Caño Harold** and **Caño Palma**. They differ in channel width, vegetation and access. Some sections are reserved for smaller, low-impact craft, so the precise route must suit both park regulations and the vessel.

Morning outings are often chosen for calmer water, gentle light and birdwatching. The [sunrise boat excursion through the Tortuguero canals](/costa-rica/tortuguero/tortuguero-dawn-canals-boat/) focuses on precisely this experience. Some programmes use kayaks instead of motorboats, offering a more active format where participants' skills and water conditions matter.

**No particular wildlife sighting is guaranteed.** Even in an animal-rich forest, encounters depend on weather, water levels, the time of day and the creatures' natural behaviour.

## When can you see sea turtles?

Tortuguero is famous for beaches where marine turtles come ashore to lay their eggs. The main viewing season for **green sea turtles** is generally **June to October**. The park authority states that the actual opening of the observation season should be checked separately, since natural events cannot be predicted to the day by a tourism calendar.

Nighttime observation is not the same as taking an independent walk on the beach. Visitors wait for permission at designated locations and only approach the animals in accordance with instructions from guides and rangers. Unrestricted beach access can disturb turtles and damage nests. Under SINAC's published regulations, night access restrictions apply on the protected beach from **1 March to 31 October**, between **18:00 and 06:00**.

Travelling to Tortuguero in season therefore **does not guarantee witnessing nesting**. Natural conditions may prevent a sighting, while administrative restrictions cannot be bypassed for a photograph. Bright lights, approaching animals and moving independently through nesting areas are unacceptable when contrary to rangers' instructions.

The park remains worthwhile outside the season: canals, birds, humid forests and guided walks offer a substantial nature experience in their own right.

## Getting there and why an overnight stay matters

Tortuguero's principal transport feature is **the waterborne part of the journey**. The road transfer to a landing stage is followed by a boat ride along rivers and canals. Our current itineraries use different landing stages: for example, on the ["Costa Rica in 5 Days" tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/), the route goes through Caño Blanco and the waterways leading to the lodge.

The particular landing, transfers and journey time depend on the transport arrangements. River levels, heavy rain and transport availability may alter arrival times. Tortuguero is therefore better planned as a dedicated overnight stop than as a brief detour between distant regions.

Pack waterproof protection for documents and electronics, a light raincoat, closed shoes and insect repellent. Weight and size restrictions may apply on boats and small aircraft; these depend on the operator and should be checked for the specific itinerary. Large suitcases are inconvenient when some transfers take place on the water.

## Choosing your programme: boat, kayak or turtle watching

| Activity | Best suited to |
|---|---|
| Motorboat | Unhurried wildlife observation |
| Canoe or kayak | More active exploration |
| Forest trail | Walking |
| Turtles at night | Seasonal, subject to regulations |

For a first visit to Tortuguero, allowing **2 nights** is practical: one for arrival and a stroll around the village, the next day for waterways and forest. Turtle watching can be added during the appropriate season only with official permission and separate confirmation of the service. Simply visiting Tortuguero does not include a night turtle excursion. This is a practical planning suggestion, not the required length of every tour.

On the ["Costa Rica in 5 Days" programme](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/), travellers explore the canals by boat before continuing to Poás and La Paz waterfalls. ["Extreme Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) features an active kayak journey through the canals followed by rafting on the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/). This distinction matters when choosing. The five-day tour is categorised as "Nature": it includes boat and forest walks, but its description does not identify a separate wildlife-spotting programme. "Extreme Costa Rica" also carries the "Animals and Safari" theme: on day 3 there is a guided kayak excursion to watch birds and other canal wildlife. Rafting on the Pacuare is a separate adventure activity, not a safari.

For a broad nature trip, compare Tortuguero with [Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/). The former centres on canals and Caribbean wetland ecosystems; the latter explores Pacific rainforest on foot. If you would like to extend the Caribbean part of your journey, consider [Puerto Viejo](/costa-rica/place/puerto-viejo/), though it requires a separate road transfer.

Find other current itineraries among our [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/). To focus on wildlife, compare [Costa Rica's "Animals and Safari" tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/); for forests, canals and waterscapes, explore the country's [nature programmes](/interests/nature/tours/costa-rica/).

## How conditions change with the seasons

The northeastern Caribbean coast is humid for much of the year. Costa Rica's general dry season from December through April does not mean there is no rain here. An itinerary needs to account for the local forecast and possible changes to water excursions, particularly after prolonged rainfall.

Turtle nesting follows its own calendar. If you are travelling specifically for this natural event, first check the season and official viewing rules, then arrange your overnight stay and transfers. If birds, forests and waterways are your main interest, your travel dates may be more flexible.

**National park admission follows SINAC regulations.** Tickets for protected routes are purchased through the official system, but the precise excursion format and additional guiding services must be checked separately. Paying a park entrance fee does not automatically include a boat excursion or turtle watching.

## Frequently asked questions about Tortuguero

### When is the best time to see turtles?

The main green sea turtle observation season runs from June to October. The presence of turtles, opening dates for viewing and access to the beach are governed by nature and park rules.

### Can you reach Tortuguero by car?

A car or bus can take you only to the appropriate landing stage. From there, the journey to the village and tourist lodges continues by water. The route depends on the itinerary and transport arrangements.

### Can you walk on the beach independently at night?

Strict restrictions apply to protected sections of the beach. During observation season, unrestricted nighttime access is prohibited or regulated; visits to turtles follow an approved procedure. Park rules take priority over any wish to photograph the animals.

### Is Tortuguero worth visiting outside nesting season?

Yes, especially if canals, birds, tropical rainforest and boat trips interest you. Turtles are just one reason to visit; the waterways and their ecosystems are fascinating throughout the year.

### Is Tortuguero suitable for swimming at the beach?

No. This is primarily a protected natural area. The authorities warn of dangerous currents in the sea and lagoons. Other parts of Costa Rica are better suited to a conventional beach holiday.

## Which tours actually travel through Tortuguero?

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} for which [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) forms part of the main itinerary. This distinction matters: travellers arrive in the canal region as a planned stage of their journey, rather than simply being offered a chance to add an excursion independently if time permits.

Tortuguero is on the Caribbean side of [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/). Unlike the volcanic areas in the country's centre or the Pacific beaches, transport here is primarily by boat. According to the conservation authority SINAC, the national park is approached via rivers and canals; ordinary road travel ends before the waterborne section.

For this reason, the number of days spent in Tortuguero is almost as important as the tour's overall length. When arrival and departure take place on separate days, there may be time for an early-morning boat excursion to spot birds, reptiles and monkeys in the forest. Actual encounters with wildlife always depend on nature.

## Short itineraries: 5–7 days

Several current programmes offer an introduction to the national park without a long holiday. They differ in where you travel after exploring the canals.

| Tour | Main difference |
|---|---|
| ["Essential Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-essentials/) | 5 days; Tortuguero, a coffee plantation and La Paz |
| ["Costa Rica in 5 Days"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/) | 5 days; Tortuguero, Poás and waterfalls |
| ["For Nature Lovers"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-for-nature-lovers/) | 6 days; Tortuguero followed by Arenal |
| ["Budget Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/budget-costa-rica/) | 7 days; Caribbean canals, Arenal, Monteverde and Manuel Antonio |

On ["Essential Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-essentials/), Tortuguero is central to the first days: travelling from San José, exploring the canals and returning to the central region. The programme then visits the Doka coffee plantation and La Paz Waterfall Gardens. This is a useful first introduction to the Caribbean forest alongside several other natural highlights.

["Costa Rica in 5 Days"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/) also sets aside a day for the national park, but its subsequent stops are different. Comparing only price and overall duration between the two five-day tours is therefore insufficient: look at each day's itinerary and choose the activities after Tortuguero that interest you more.

["Costa Rica for Nature Lovers"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-for-nature-lovers/) continues towards [Arenal and La Fortuna](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). ["Budget Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/budget-costa-rica/) covers a wider region: the Caribbean canals are followed by volcanic landscapes, cloud forests and Manuel Antonio National Park. Transfer times are particularly important on such an extensive route.

## 10–16-day itineraries: combining natural regions

For travellers hoping to discover several of Costa Rica's ecosystems, Tortuguero combines well with volcanic slopes, cloud forests and the ocean coast.

["Pearls of Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-pearls-10-days/) is a ten-day itinerary where Tortuguero's canals provide one of the first major nature experiences. Travellers then visit Arenal, other volcanic and forest areas, and the coast. This suits those seeking varied scenery and activities rather than spending several days at a single park.

["Best of Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/best-of-costa-rica/) offers a longer introduction to the country. Tortuguero is combined with Arenal and other regions; choose the trip according to its complete list of stops and each day's activities, not simply the name of one well-known national park.

On ["Extreme Costa Rica"](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), the quiet canals at the start give way to rafting on the Pacuare River and activities around Arenal and Monteverde. This is a different kind of product: nature sightseeing is combined with physical challenges. Sharing Tortuguero as a stop does not make the tours equivalent.

The ["Premium Costa Rica Tour, 16 Days"](/costa-rica/tour/luxury-costa-rica-16-days/) includes Tortuguero in an extended journey through volcanoes, forests, the Osa Peninsula and the beaches of Playa Conchal. The word "premium" alone does not guarantee a particular boat type, a dedicated naturalist or private access to the park. Confirm these services against the actual programme and accommodation conditions.

## Tortuguero on a multi-country journey

The park also appears on itineraries where Costa Rica is only one part of the trip. On the ["Costa Rica–Nicaragua" tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/), Tortuguero is one of the nature-focused stages in Costa Rica, followed by other destinations. The sequence of transfers and border-crossing documents should be agreed in advance.

On the [26-day journey through eight Central American countries](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), Tortuguero comes towards the end: day 22 involves arrival from the Arenal area, day 23 a dawn cruise through the canals, and day 24 a return via San José followed by a flight to Panama. It illustrates how the park can fit naturally into an extensive international itinerary while still requiring dedicated time for the boat transfer.

If Tortuguero itself is your priority, first compare the shorter [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/). A lengthy multi-country journey is chosen for its overall geography, not just a few additional hours in one park.

## How you arrive and how much time to allow for the canals

Typical local logistics involve a road journey from San José or another city to a landing stage, then a boat trip. However, the precise boarding point, operator, schedule and transfer type depend on the itinerary. What looks close on a map may not be close in travel time: the distance to the canals is not the time needed to reach a lodge or the national park.

A good plan allows for an early outing on the water. This lets you observe the forest and waterways before the busiest boat traffic, although weather may alter departure times. Some sections permit canoes and kayaks; others use motorboats. The vessel and route must comply with park regulations and the services actually included.

Check how many nights the programme allocates specifically to Tortuguero. An arrival day followed by departure does not provide the same viewing time as an itinerary with a full morning on the canals. Also confirm whether park admission, a local guide and the boat trip form part of the package.

## When to visit for turtles, birds and rainforest

Tortuguero is a nature destination throughout the year, but different experiences are seasonal. SINAC identifies **June–October** as the main period for observing sea turtle nesting on regulated visits. A sighting on a particular night is not guaranteed, and access rules for the beach are set by the conservation authority.

Night turtle watching is a separate protected activity. It is not automatically included in every itinerary that mentions Tortuguero; the season, permitted form of visit and accompanying specialist must be taken into account. At other times of year, the canals, birds, amphibians, reptiles and rainforest make the journey worthwhile.

For boat and land excursions, pack lightweight clothing, a raincoat, closed shoes, insect protection and waterproof packaging for documents. Heavy rain is possible on the Caribbean coast even during what is commonly described as Costa Rica's dry season. Swell, water levels and conservation restrictions affect access to individual areas.

## How to compare prices and included services

Two Tortuguero tours may vary substantially in price even when they last about the same length of time. Differences come from what follows the park, accommodation standards and location, the number of transfers, the excursion programme and which services are prepaid. A tour title alone cannot tell you what meals are included, the room category or whether a boat excursion is private.

Compare the offers using a few questions: how many days are spent at the park, which boat route is planned, is an early-morning excursion included, where does the trip go after Tortuguero, and how much time is spent travelling? Only then compare published conditions and costs on an equivalent basis: per person, per group or per programme.

If Tortuguero is essential, compare the actual itineraries in this selection. For a wider nature-focused trip, consider the [Costa Rica wildlife tour collection](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/), where Tortuguero is one possible highlight.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I reach Tortuguero by car?

Road transfers reach the appropriate landing stage, after which boats are used within the park region. The boarding location and journey time depend on the chosen programme and waterway conditions.

### Do the tours always show sea turtles?

No. Nesting observations depend on season, weather and conservation regulations. A visit to Tortuguero means the tour covers the region, but does not guarantee seeing turtles or include a paid nighttime beach excursion.

### Is a five-day tour enough to see the park?

Yes, short programmes provide a first introduction to the canals and wildlife. Check how many hours are spent in Tortuguero itself, however: on some five-day trips, travel from and back to San José takes a substantial amount of time.

### Which is better: Tortuguero and Arenal or Tortuguero and the coast?

Combining Tortuguero with [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) suits travellers who want volcanic landscapes and thermal areas after the Caribbean canals. An itinerary that adds the Pacific coast offers beaches and a different natural environment, usually on a longer journey.

### Do I need a separate boat excursion if my tour already passes through the park?

That depends on the specific programme. Some tours list a boat trip in the day-by-day itinerary, while others require clarification of the visiting arrangements. Check whether a boat, tickets, a guide and any early-morning excursion are included in your chosen [tour](/costa-rica/tour/).

## Viento Fresco Waterfalls: a nature stop between Arenal and Monteverde

**Viento Fresco is a group of waterfalls among green mountain slopes near Tilarán in Costa Rica.** It is a convenient nature stop on the road between [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Monteverde's cloud forests](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Walking trails lead to the falls, with stairways, descents and viewpoints along the way.

Choosing the correct site is particularly important here. ## What you can see at the waterfalls

The waterfalls lie in a forested mountain setting. The walking route offers flowing water, rocky streambeds, moss on damp stones and surrounding pastures or wooded slopes. Some sections of the complex contain small natural pools, but whether swimming is safe depends on water levels and the rules at the particular site.

A popular route features several distinct cascades, including Arco Iris Waterfall. Some descents have steep steps. **Going down and climbing back up require different levels of effort**: after a quick photograph beside the water, you still need to climb back, so allow time and energy for the return.

A general view of a waterfall may be available from one spot, while reaching its base requires another approach. Ask the staff which sections are open and what kind of walk is appropriate for your fitness.

The trail can become slippery after heavy rain. Choose a time that leaves ample daylight and does not require rushing to your next hotel.

## What to bring

Wear closed shoes with good grip, carry drinking water and light rain protection. Use handrails on wet steps and avoid cliff edges just to take a photograph.

If you intend to swim, confirm in advance which natural pools are actually open. Currents at waterfalls change with water levels, and swimming close to a powerful cascade or jumping from rocks is dangerous.

Mist and rain are possible in mountainous Costa Rica even when the coast is sunny. Weather near Tilarán does not always match the forecast for the nearest major city.
